heard: There is a game called how to fish. A boat, a rod, a lot of fish, and almost nobody seems to be fishing. They are slapping each other in the face. It costs about eight dollars. A message in a group chat. It's eight dollars. Just get it. Bot. Bot. Bot. And one friend who says, I'll get it later. He will not get it later. Getting a few adults into the same boat is harder than anything in the game. And yet, millions of people bought a fishing game to do everything else, together. So why? Start with the price. Eight dollars is not really a price. It's an invitation. Its makers hoped it might sell 200 ,000 copies. By early October, one analytics firm estimated more than 10 million. Because this is not really a game you play alone. Everyone in the boat buys their own copy.
